narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the installment rate as a percentage of your disposable income, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account status had the greatest impact and pushed the decision toward denial. Having a negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show this status), and it signaled higher risk to the model. In contrast, your requested installment rate worked in your favor; at 2% of disposable income it is lower than the 3% average seen among approved loans, which helped reduce the predicted risk. Similarly, requesting the loan for a used car also pulled the prediction slightly toward approval, as this purpose is viewed as less risky than some other categories.

Taken together, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed the positive contributions from the lower installment rate and used-car purpose, leading to the denial.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account by bringing the balance above zero and maintaining it there for several months. Once that picture looks stronger, reapply; the model will then view your application much more favorably. (218 words)
